events.title: Future Queen Victoria is born
events.description: Alexandrina Victoria was born at Kensington Palace in London. She became queen in 1837 at age 18 and reigned for more than 63 years.
events.significance: Her reign gave its name to the Victorian era, a period of industrial expansion, imperial growth and social change in Britain.

events.title: Morse sends the first telegraph message between cities
events.description: Samuel F. B. Morse tapped out the message "What hath God wrought" from the U.S. Capitol in Washington to Baltimore. It formally opened America's first telegraph line.
events.significance: The telegraph made rapid long-distance communication possible and paved the way for today's global communications networks.

events.title: Brooklyn Bridge opens
events.description: The Brooklyn Bridge opened to traffic, linking Manhattan and Brooklyn across the East River. At the time it was the longest suspension bridge in the world.
events.significance: It was a landmark of civil engineering and became an enduring symbol of New York City.

events.title: HMS Hood sunk by the Bismarck
events.description: In the Battle of the Denmark Strait, the German battleship Bismarck sank the British battlecruiser HMS Hood. Only three of her crew survived.
events.significance: The loss of the Royal Navy's most famous warship shocked Britain. It set off the pursuit that ended with the Bismarck's sinking days later.
